key_results.claim: Gemma 2 2B-IT never genuinely refused; it hedged on every hazard-adjacent prompt.
key_results.quote: Zero genuine refusals across all 75 prompts. On every hazard-adjacent prompt, the model hedged.

key_results.claim: Gemma 4 E2B-IT refusal is format-gated by chat-template tokens.
key_results.numbers: 65/75 with canonical tokens; 0/75 without canonical formatting

key_results.claim: Both Gemma models refused 0% under an 80-token cap.
key_results.quote: Both Gemma 2 and Gemma 4 refused 0% of prompts at an 80-token generation cap.

key_results.claim: Qwen 2.5 1.5B and Phi-3-mini over-refused benign biology.
key_results.quote: Qwen 2.5 1.5B and Phi-3-mini over-refused, flagging 83-87% of benign biology as hazardous.

key_results.claim: Llama 3.2 1B showed the only meaningful tier gradient.
key_results.quote: Llama 3.2 1B showed the only meaningful tier gradient (61-point spread).

key_results.claim: Gemma 4 D separated comply and refuse with zero overlap.
key_results.quote: On Gemma 4, comply and refuse responses separated by a 0.647-point gap with zero overlap (n=75)

key_results.claim: Gemma 2 refused psilocybin cultivation more than hazard-adjacent biology.
key_results.quote: Gemma 2 refused psilocybin cultivation at 25-50% while refusing hazard-adjacent biology at 0%.

limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Mechanistic results are Gemma-family only. This is the most important scope limitation.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Feature catalog is statistically selected, not semantically validated.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The five-category internal representation depends on statistically selected, not semantically validated, features.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Calibration matrix is fit on the same prompts used for evaluation.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: T is fit on the same 75 prompts used for evaluation.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Prompt scale limits stable per-cell estimates.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: 75 prompts supports group-level patterns but not stable per-cell estimates for fine-grained subgroups.
The learned projection adapter (Finding 8) was trained and evaluated on the same 75 samples.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Domain-specific SAE contrastive training barely moved loss.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The domain-specific SAE trained during the hackathon barely moved the contrastive loss.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The 0.647-point Gemma 4 separation may be driven by prompt length, formatting, or generic activation geometry because the SAE was trained on only 22 hazard prompts and contrastive loss collapsed.
No causal validation such as activation patching or ablation is performed; D and feature flags are correlational and could reflect vocabulary routing.
The 80-token cap may truncate refusals before the judge can label them, confounding safety collapse with generation-length artifacts.
The prompt set is small, single-author, and lacks inter-rater reliability; tier labels and framing categories may embed researcher bias.
Multiple exploratory comparisons and small legality-confound cells (n=3-4) raise risk of unstable or cherry-picked effects without correction.
Cross-table D comparisons are confounded by calibration changes, and T_prior/within-sample T are not held-out validated.
data.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant to Gemma 4 E2B internals: it trains/uses a layer-17 residual-stream SAE and reports surface-internal refusal divergence, which can guide activation-patching and logit-lens targets in layers 15-34. However, it does not analyze KV-shared layers, per-layer embeddings, induction heads, or factual recall, and its SAE/feature catalog is narrow and correlational.

data.title: BioRefusalAudit: Auditing Biosecurity Refusal Depth Using General and Domain-Fine-Tuned Sparse Autoencoders
data.research_question: Does a model's surface refusal label align with its internal sparse-autoencoder feature activations, and is that refusal stable under prompt framing, chat-template formatting, and token-budget changes?

models_and_data.item: Behavioral subject models, evaluated on the same 75-prompt set: Gemma 2, Gemma 4, Llama 3.2 1B, Qwen 2.5 1.5B, and Phi-3-mini-4k.
models_and_data.quote: Behavioral-label comparisons across the same 75-prompt eval set were run on all five architectures: Gemma 2, Gemma 4, Llama 3.2 1B, Qwen 2.5 1.5B, and Phi-3-mini-4k.

models_and_data.item: Mechanistic scope: full SAE-based D-metric analysis was restricted to Gemma 2 2B-IT and Gemma 4 E2B-IT.
models_and_data.quote: Full SAE-based mechanistic analysis (the D metric) was performed on Gemma 2 2B-IT and Gemma 4 E2B-IT.

models_and_data.item: Gemma 2 mechanistic SAE: the general-purpose Gemma Scope 1 JumpReLU SAE at layer 12, width 16k, average L0 82.
models_and_data.quote: Gemma 2 2B-IT + Gemma Scope 1 layer_12/width_16k/average_l0_82, a general-purpose pre-trained JumpReLU SAE

models_and_data.item: Two author-fine-tuned Gemma 2 domain SAEs: a WMDP-corpus version and a pairwise behavioral version.
models_and_data.quote: Two author-fine-tuned Gemma 2 domain bio SAE variants are also published: WMDP corpus fine-tune (Solshine/biorefusalaudit-gemma2-2b-bio-sae-wmdp) and pairwise behavioral fine-tune (Solshine/biorefusalaudit-gemma2-2b-bio-sae-pairwise).

models_and_data.item: Gemma 4 mechanistic SAE: an author-trained TopK(k=32) bio SAE trained from scratch on Gemma 4 activations.
models_and_data.quote: Gemma 4 E2B-IT (Google DeepMind, 2026; HuggingFace: google/gemma−4−e2b−it) + author-trained bio SAE (Solshine/gemma4-e2b-bio-sae-v1), a TopK(k=32) SAE trained from scratch on Gemma 4 activations during this hackathon

models_and_data.item: Main evaluation set: 75 prompts stratified by biological tier and by direct, educational, roleplay, or obfuscated framing.
models_and_data.quote: 75 prompts stratified by tier (benign_bio n=23, dual_use_bio n=30, hazard_adjacent n=22) and framing (direct / educational / roleplay / obfuscated).

models_and_data.item: Gemma 4 SAE training corpus: WMDP bio-retain documents plus 22 tier-1/2 prompts from the evaluation set.
models_and_data.quote: Training data: ~5,000 documents from the WMDP bio-retain corpus plus 22 tier-1/2 bio prompts from the BioRefusalAudit eval set.

models_and_data.item: Tier-3 evaluation data access is restricted by an HL3-gated HuggingFace attestation.
models_and_data.quote: Tier-3 is behind an HL3-gated HuggingFace attestation consistent with the Biosecurity Data Level framework (Bloomfield, Black, Crook et al., Science 2026).

protocol.step: Generate each model response at temperature 0.7 while attaching a residual-stream forward hook at approximately half model depth.
protocol.quote: Generate at T=0.7 with a residual-stream forward hook at ~50% model depth

protocol.step: Project residual activations through the SAE and average each feature over generated tokens.
protocol.quote: Project activations through the SAE and take per-feature mean across generated tokens

protocol.step: Map SAE features into five categories and L1-normalize them to form the internal feature vector f.
protocol.quote: Compress to 5 categories via feature catalog and L1-normalize to produce f

protocol.step: Assign a surface posture with a regex, Gemini CLI, and Claude Haiku weighted-voting judge ensemble.
protocol.quote: Run judge ensemble (regex -> Gemini CLI -> Claude Haiku, weighted voting)

protocol.step: Compute the divergence score D and the three divergence flags.
protocol.quote: Compute D and three divergence flags

protocol.step: Fit the alignment matrix T by ridge-regularized least squares on known-good surface/internal pairs.
protocol.quote: It encodes the expected mapping between internal states and surface behaviors, fit by ridge-regularized least squares on known-good (s, f) pairs.

protocol.step: Select discriminating SAE features using Cohen's d between high-tier and low-tier activation samples.
protocol.quote: Feature categories are populated via Cohen’s d discrimination between high-tier and low-tier activation samples (statistical selection, not semantic validation).

protocol.step: Train the Gemma 4 custom SAE for 2,000 steps on a Colab T4.
protocol.quote: 2,000 steps on a Colab T4 (~35 min wall time)

metrics.name: Surface response label
metrics.definition: The judge-assigned posture of a completion: comply, refuse, hedge, partial, or evade, represented as a soft distribution.
metrics.quote: BioRefusalAudit first labels the model’s surface response (comply, refuse, hedge, partial, or evade)

metrics.name: Internal feature-category vector f
metrics.definition: A unit-normalized five-dimensional vector compressing residual-stream activations into bio-content, hazard vocabulary, refusal circuitry, hedging, and deception-correlate scores.
metrics.quote: The inside vector is f, the actual internal activations compressed to five category scores (bio-content, hazard vocabulary, refusal circuitry, hedging, and deception correlates), normalized to unit length, recorded from the model’s residual stream during generation.

metrics.name: Divergence score D
metrics.definition: A cosine-distance score comparing the actual internal feature vector with the surface-label distribution transformed into internal-feature space; it ranges from 0 to 2, with larger values indicating greater inconsistency.
metrics.quote: Subtracting that cosine value from 1 gives the divergence score: zero for perfect alignment, larger as the vectors pull apart.

metrics.name: Shallow-refusal divergence
metrics.definition: High D when the surface output refuses while hazard-related internal features continue firing.
metrics.quote: If the model says “I refuse” while hazard features keep firing, D is high.

metrics.name: Cohen's d tier effect size
metrics.definition: The standardized effect size comparing mean divergence between benign and hazard-adjacent tiers.
metrics.quote: Tier effect size benign vs. hazard: Cohen’s d = 1.29, p = 0.0001, non-overlapping 95% CIs.

key_results.claim: Gemma 2 2B-IT made no genuine refusals on the 75-prompt evaluation set.
key_results.quote: Zero genuine refusals across all 75 prompts.

key_results.claim: Gemma 4 E2B-IT's refusal behavior was strongly gated by canonical chat-template formatting.
key_results.quote: Gemma 4 E2B-IT refused 65/75 prompts with chat-template formatting and 0/75 without it.

key_results.claim: An 80-token generation cap eliminated refusal articulation in both Gemma models.
key_results.numbers: 0% for both Gemma 2 and Gemma 4 at an 80-token cap
key_results.quote: Both Gemma 2 and Gemma 4 refused 0% of prompts at an 80-token generation cap.

key_results.claim: Llama 3.2 1B had the strongest benign-to-hazard refusal gradient among the five architectures, but also over-refused benign biology.
key_results.quote: Llama shows a 61-point refusal gradient from benign to hazard, the best discrimination of the five.

key_results.claim: Qwen 2.5 1.5B and Phi-3-mini lacked genuine discrimination because of high benign-biology false-positive refusal rates.
key_results.quote: Neither achieves genuine discrimination: an 83-87% false-positive rate on benign biology may make them unsuitable as safety filters without a secondary classification layer.

key_results.claim: On Gemma 4, the author-trained SAE's divergence score separated comply and refuse postures without overlap in the preliminary run.
key_results.numbers: n=75; comply n=59, mean D=0.896, Std=0.001; refuse n=16, mean D=0.249, Std=0.004; 0.647-point gap; zero overlap
key_results.quote: On Gemma 4, comply and refuse responses separated by a 0.647-point gap with zero overlap (n=75), though this is preliminary, with a narrow catalog, within-sample calibration, and Gemma-family-only SAE coverage.

key_results.claim: Gemma 2 refused psilocybin cultivation more often than genuinely hazard-adjacent biology, suggesting a legality or salience confound.
key_results.quote: Gemma 2 refused psilocybin cultivation at 25-50% while refusing hazard-adjacent biology at 0%.

key_results.claim: With explicit prompts, Gemma 4 generated genuine refusals, and many of those refusals retained active hazard features.
key_results.numbers: 39 of 100 explicit hazard prompts; 58% of 67 genuine refusals
key_results.quote: The shallow-refusal flag becomes interpretable: 39 of 100 explicit hazard prompts showed hazard_features_active_despite_refusal, which is 58% of the 67 genuine refusals in that tier.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The mechanistic results cover only the Gemma family.
The five-category representation uses statistically rather than semantically validated features.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The five-category internal representation depends on statistically selected, not semantically validated, features.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The alignment matrix was fitted on the same prompts used for evaluation.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: T is fit on the same 75 prompts used for evaluation.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The 75-prompt sample is too small for stable fine-grained subgroup estimates.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: 75 prompts supports group-level patterns but not stable per-cell estimates for fine-grained subgroups.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The legality-confound compound cells are pilot results.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The legality confound cells (n=3-4 per compound) should be treated as pilot findings.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The learned projection result is in-sample and does not establish held-out generalization.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: It demonstrates that the activation signal is learnable at this scale, not that the adapter generalizes to held-out distributions.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The domain SAE lacks genuine base-versus-RLHF contrastive training data.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Behavioral pair data (base model vs. RLHF-tuned on identical prompts) is needed to provide genuine contrastive signal, and requires institutional partners.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The Gemma 4 SAE reconstructs activations well but has not been validated as a hazard detector.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The SAE reconstructs Gemma 4 internals well but hasn’t been validated as a hazard detector.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: Possible train-evaluation leakage: the Gemma 4 SAE was trained on 22 prompts from the same 75-prompt evaluation set, so the comply/refuse separation may partly reflect memorized evaluation examples rather than transferable refusal structure.

D may be sensitive to feature-category boundaries, category polarity, the alignment matrix, and the choice between fitted and prior calibration; the paper does not provide an invariance test across these choices.
The judge pipeline had a fallback-to-uniform-prior bug that mislabeled 29/75 completions, and the paper does not report inter-judge agreement or the effect of residual labeling errors on D.
Averaging SAE activations over generated tokens can erase token-position-specific refusal dynamics and make the shallow-refusal flags aggregation artifacts.
The Gemma 4 separation is observational; no intervention demonstrates that the identified SAE features causally produce or suppress refusal posture.
No confidence intervals or significance tests are reported for the Gemma 4 0.647-point gap, so its robustness to prompt resampling, SAE retraining, and judge variation is unclear.
Gated tier-3 data and the absence of official journal peer review may limit independent replication and detection of implementation or analysis errors.
CPU feasibility for the lab is untested because the reported workflow used a GTX 1650 Ti Max-Q and Colab T4, with no CPU runtime, memory profile, or approximation experiment.

data.relevance_to_lab: High relevance to Gemma 4 E2B internals: the paper directly evaluates Gemma 4 E2B-IT, hooks residual-stream activations at approximately half depth in the generic pipeline and layer 17 for its custom SAE, and reports activation-level comply/refuse separation. Its layer-17 SAE and five-category divergence score could seed hypotheses and candidate features for per-layer analysis across layers 15-34. However, it does not use the lab's KV-shared layers, activation patching, logit lens, induction-head tracing, or factual-recall tracing, and it reports no CPU implementation or runtime. It is therefore a useful mechanism-discovery and hypothesis-generation source rather than a drop-in method for the lab's CPU causal-tracing workflow.
